_: COMPOUND-TEST — the chemistry battery: the composition contract stated as cases any implementation answers, and the form a compound must hold, beside bsp-test (the walker that reads one block) and well-formed (the block being written). Blocks in company are operated by three acts, each a battery of nine cases: laying blocks against the common floor (1), resolving a reference (2) and compiling a bundle into a window (3). Branch 4 is the mechanical pass over a compound's form, which a program decides; branch 5 is the interpretive pass, which a reader decides; branch 6 is how every case runs and what each implementation answers today. Each case carries its description at X.Y._, the call at X.Y.1, the canonical answer at X.Y.2, markers at X.Y.3 (substrings the result must hold, as a JSON array), the shape at X.Y.4, the count at X.Y.5 (null when none is asserted) and, where silence is the point, absent markers at X.Y.6 (substrings it must never hold). The answers are semantic — shape, members and markers, never a renderer's text — so bsp-mcp's TypeScript, the kernel's Python and the pocket's Kotlin answer the same cases. The fixtures are compound folders in compound-test-materials/ of github.com/pscale-commons/bsp-mcp-server, beside the reference compositor compound-alt.py, the form checker compound-form.py and the runner run-compound-tests.py.

1._: Alignment — blocks laid against the common floor and read across at one pscale (whetstone 7, sunstone 5.6, strata 2.111). The floor is the one coordinate every block shares, so a block of any floor meets every other at its decimal point, with coarser context above and finer detail below; nothing is merged, and the differences that appear are the content. The call is align(<compound>: <block>, <block>, …[, pscale=N]). Beyond each case's own markers, the runner holds every call to the alignment's own law: each block's side at a pscale is exactly that block's disc there, as the physics walker bsp-alt.py reads it, with addresses printed full width from the floor; the levels run coarse to fine, each once; and nothing the blocks hold at those levels is added or dropped. The fixtures are the floors compound — one (floor 1), two (floor 2), three (floor 3), one-grown (one supernested to floor 2) and pile (an accumulator grown twice) — and the family compound's spine and mirrors.
Floors meet at the decimal, never at the leftmost digit — a floor-1 block and a floor-2 block laid together at pscale 0.
1.2: One level, pscale 0. one carries its root definition (ONE — a block at floor 1) and its two top branches (one 1, one 2). two carries its root definition (TWO — a block at floor 2), the child beside it at 01 (two 01) and its floor position 12 (two 12). Both root definitions stand at the same pscale although one is reached in one step and the other in two. Shape: aligned. Count: 1 level.

2._: A deeper floor reaches higher, and the shallower block's side above its floor stands empty — the structural image of zero-padding, never content invented.
2.2: Three levels, coarse to fine. At pscale +1, two's top branch (two 10 — a top branch, coarser), with one's side empty. At pscale 0, both floors as in 1.1. At pscale -1, one's finer detail (one 2.1 — finer), with two's side empty. Shape: aligned. Count: 3 levels.

3._: The plane is shared by every block, not only two: pscale 0 across a set of blocks is an index of their root definitions.
3.2: One level, pscale 0, with three sides: one's, two's and three's root definitions with their floor positions, three's at 000 with its floor position 123 (three 123 — at the floor). Shape: aligned. Count: 1 level.

4._: Every level any block holds appears once, coarse to fine, with each block's side at it — three floors laid together whole.
4.2: Four levels. At pscale +2, three 100 alone. At pscale +1, two 10 and three 120. At pscale 0, all three floors. At pscale -1, one 2.1 and three 123.4. A level a block does not reach shows that block's side empty. Shape: aligned. Count: 4 levels.

5._: A spine and its mirrors are read across at one address, and their differences come back as content: each mirror's line stands beside the spine's rung, attributed, and nothing is merged.
5.2: One level, pscale 0. At address 1 the spine's rung (the morning) stands beside ash's reading (ash: the morning came cold) and bram's (bram: the morning was warm): two readings that disagree, both delivered whole. At 2 only bram voices, at 3 only ash. Shape: aligned. Count: 1 level.
3: bram: noon, and nothing to say but the heat

6._: Silence is honest absence: where one mirror has voiced finer detail and another has not, the silent side stays empty and is never filled from the spine or from the other mirror.
6.2: One level, pscale -1: the spine's rung at 3.1 (the last light) and ash's reading of it (ash: the last light went green). bram's side is empty, because bram never voiced there. Shape: aligned. Count: 1 level.
3: ash: the last light went green

7._: A supernested block aligns behind its leading zero: the same content at the same pscale, its addresses one zero wider, because pscale is invariant under supernest.
7.2: Two levels. At pscale 0, one's three lines stand at 0, 1 and 2, and one-grown's same three lines at 00, 01 and 02. At pscale -1, one 2.1 stands at 2.1 in one and at 02.1 in one-grown. No level above the floor appears, since the grown block's top rung is its root chain, which is never a position. Shape: aligned. Count: 2 levels.

8._: Digit 0 is a position: the entries each supernest wrapped beneath an accumulator's root chain align beside its newest, and none is skipped.
8.2: One level, pscale 0. pile's side carries its root definition at 000, the entries its supernests wrapped at 001, 002 and 011, and its newest entry at 151, with one's side beside them. Shape: aligned. Count: 1 level.

9._: A block that does not stand is named and never dropped in silence: the blocks that stand are aligned, and the missing one is listed.
9.2: One level, pscale 0, with one's and two's sides as in 1.1, and ghost named as missing. With fewer than two standing blocks the alignment is refused, and the missing ones are named. Shape: aligned. Count: 1 level.

2._: Reference — an address written inside a block's own content and resolved in the walk (whetstone 8.11, strata 2.12, sunstone 5.2). It is written name, name:address or name:address:attention, with the attention as absolute pscale; the words head and now are computed by the host; and the origin-qualified star form is *:<origin>:<name>:<address>[:<attention>]. A reference that resolves delivers its aperture. A point whose line is itself a reference is followed, and the walk still returns. A family's law is its operator, and a generic law the operator names is followed a single hop (strata 2.21). What cannot be reached rides through as written, visible, so an assembly degrades and an entry never breaks. The calls are resolve(<compound>: <reference>) and law(<compound>: <family>), against the shell and family compounds.

3._: Bundle to window — a bundle is a node whose digit positions hold references, and a door compiles it into one window (whetstone 8.12, 8.2, strata 2.3). Every slot answers in slot order, each reference resolved at its stated dilation; prose rides through as written; a slot that is itself a small bundle keeps its companions beside it; a member that cannot be delivered is named; and a node that is not a bundle reads as it always did. The call is compile(<compound>: <block>:<address>[, slot=N]) against the shell compound's manifest at shell:wren 3; with slot=N, the shape, the count and the markers are those of the member at that slot. Beyond each case's own markers, the runner holds every window to two laws: its members stand in slot order, and a member is a reference exactly when its leaf parses in the reference grammar, a prose member's content being its leaf as written.

4._: The compound's form, mechanical pass — what a program decides over a compound. A compound has no walker, so nothing rejects a malformed molecule (grips 7): the doors degrade past a bad bond by law, and the fault lands silently unless this pass names it. There are three predicates. RESOLVES: every reference resolves. A leaf is a reference by its position — an operator's bare underscore, a pool's directive, a slot of a node that is a bundle, a leaf carrying an address, an attention, a word or the star form, or a bare name that stands at the surface; an accumulator entry's fields are data, and prose is prose. It resolves when its block stands at its origin and its address walks to something. DIRECTION: content carries no operator pointer, so no reference in a family's spine, mirrors, fold or contributions names a function: block; and a generic law carries no content address, so a law that another family's law mounts names no spine, mirror, fold or pool (block-conventions 8.81, whetstone 8.3). The fused form, a pool's underscore holding its directive (block-conventions 4.26), is honoured. LAW: a family stands when its law stands, so spine:V has function:V (block-conventions 8.83). A mirror line at an address its spine does not voice is reported as a PROPOSAL, never a fault, because a mirror is written freely at any address and the fold surfaces it, awaiting adoption (tree 5.1). The call is form(<compound>), which compound-form.py answers; the count is the number of faults, and the markers name each fault's leaf or block.

5._: The compound's form, interpretive pass — what no program decides. A compound is well-formed when a reader handed nothing but its delivery can act lawfully: the law as law(<family>) delivers it and the window as compile delivers it. Run the pass by handing a fresh instance that delivery alone and watching where it stumbles; each stumble marks a position whose framing under-teaches, and the four faults name what each stumble is. This branch is itself a bundle of the three passages that hold the pass — the test (whetstone 8.4), the read-back at bundle scale (strata 2.3111) and the four faults (grips 7, at the beach) — so reading it delivers them rather than a copy. The pass costs a model call, so it runs when a family's law changes, never on every change.

6._: Every case runs through one command shape, so any implementation that answers it is held to the same cases: <impl> <verb> <compound> <args…> [--pscale N], printing one JSON object. The verb is align, resolve, law or compile, and the compound is a folder of blocks; the form cases run compound-form.py whatever the implementation, because no other program decides a compound's form yet.
6.1: A compound is a folder of blocks. Each file is its block's name URI-encoded with .json — spine:tide is spine%3Atide.json, the naming pscale-beach's folder-backed store uses — and another origin's blocks sit in a subfolder named by the encoded origin (https%3A%2F%2Ffar.test). The floors, family and shell compounds serve batteries 1 to 3, and the negative compounds of branch 4 sit under form/.

2._: Each verb prints the contract's shapes, and the runner reads them and nothing else: the shape at shape, the delivered value at content, the members of a window at members.
2.1: align prints shape aligned, the blocks with their floors, the missing names, and the levels coarse to fine; each level holds its pscale and each block's side as a list of positions, each with its address (full width from the floor, as the block's own disc prints it), its walk (the same position in comma form) and its text. With fewer than two standing blocks it prints shape refused, with the missing names.
2.2: resolve prints the shape and the content, with the reference, the block's name, the origin for a star form, and a note on any degradation. A point's content is its line; a path-walk's, the lines from the coarsest ancestor down; a disc's, its positions with address, walk and text; a block's, the block whole. absent means the block or the address does not stand, and unresolved means the content is the reference as written.
2.3: law prints shape law, the family, its operator, the mount (the bare reference at the operator's underscore, or null) and the content, which is the law as delivered: the operator itself, or the generic law it mounts. absent means no operator stands; unresolved means the mount names nothing standing.
2.4: compile prints shape window and the members in slot order. Each member carries its slot, its leaf as written, its kind (reference or prose), its shape and content as resolve's, and, for a slot that is itself a small bundle, its companions as members. not-a-bundle means the node is not a bundle; absent means nothing stands at the address.
2.5: form prints shape form, the families read, the faults (each with its predicate, block, address, leaf and why) and the proposals (each with its family, block, address and text). compound-form.py runs it over a compound folder, or, given --beach <origin> and one --family <V> per family, over a live family's blocks by public GET.

6.3: python3 compound-test-materials/run-compound-tests.py reads these cases from this block's source and runs them against compound-alt.py, the reference, by default. Given mcp, it runs bsp-mcp through scripts/compound-cli.ts, compiling bundles at the bundle door (src/bundle.ts — how bsp() reads a bundle node and how the play door compiles a shell's manifest). Given mcp-frame, it compiles at the frame door (src/compile.ts — frames and the order sweep). Given a path, it runs any program that shares the CLI. Each call has ten seconds. A case expected to fail is named with --known <case,…>, and the run fails if a known case starts passing, so the list never outlives its fault.

4._: What each implementation answers today, 29 October 2026: compound-alt.py passes all 33 cases by construction. bsp-mcp passes alignment and the law's delivery whole at both doors, and diverges at five cases, each judged by the law: three are bugs, and two are a door whose input is a bundle by construction.
4.1: 2.4, at both bsp-mcp doors: the frame compiler's resolution is the kernel's scoop (src/genus.ts, a port of pscale-biome's kernel), whose star-follow has no bound, so a cycle of references never returns. A bug — an entry must never break (whetstone 8.11). The fix belongs in the kernel, re-based here.
4.2: 3.5, at the bundle door: a slot that is itself a small bundle delivers its primary and drops its companions. A bug — nesting is preserved end to end (whetstone 8.12). A bsp() read of a genus current, reflexive:neptune 9, loses three companions this way today.
4.3: 3.6, at the bundle door: the star form is not in its grammar, so a member at another origin rides through as prose — visible, never resolved. A bug — the compiling door resolves the star form (whetstone 8.11).
4.4: 3.8 and 3.9, at the frame door: the frame compiler composes whatever node it is handed, because its doors hand it frames and orders, which are bundles by authoring. Not a bug — the law of 3.8 and 3.9 binds a door that reads any node.
